title: El Mundial
focus: Preterite vs. imperfect, and verbs that change meaning

slots.puerta: Jodi's guide · same family as Puertas 2 and 4
slots.mis: "Preterite and imperfect both just mean past"

slots.skill: tenía (had, a state) vs. tuvo (got, an event)
slots.mis: "Preterite and imperfect both just mean past"
Uses the preterite for what was going on
Uses conocía for a first meeting

slots.skill: Tell a short past story with both tenses
slots.mis: Swaps the scene and the event

A.q:
“Yesterday I found out there was a game.”
Ayer ___ que había un partido.
A.why: Finding something out happens once: supe. Sabía means you already knew.

A.q:
“When I was a kid, Diego had a dog named Tango.”
De niño, Diego ___ un perro que se llamaba Tango.
A.why: Having a dog for years is a state, so tenía. Tuvo would mean he got one.

A.q:
“While Lucía was sleeping, the train stopped in Vladimir.”
Mientras Lucía ___, el tren paró en Vladimir.
A.why: Sleeping is the background; stopping is the event that happened during it.

A.q:
“Yesterday at the museum I met an artist from Lima.”
Ayer en el museo ___ a una artista de Lima.
A.why: Meeting someone for the first time is one event: conocí.

A.q: Which sentence tells it right? “It was sunny when we got to the beach.”
o: Hacía sol cuando llegamos a la playa.
Hizo sol cuando llegábamos a la playa.
A.why: The weather is the scene (hacía); arriving is the event (llegamos).

B.q:
“This morning I found out the train was leaving late.”
Esta mañana ___ que el tren salía tarde.
B.why: Finding out is one moment: supe. Sabía would mean you knew all along.

B.q:
“When we left the hotel, I had my passport in my backpack.”
Cuando salimos del hotel, yo ___ el pasaporte en la mochila.
B.why: The passport was in the bag the whole time: a state, so tenía.

B.q:
“While we were eating, it started to rain.”
Mientras nosotros ___, empezó a llover.
B.why: Eating is the background; the rain starting is the event.

B.q:
“At the party last night I met Facu's brother.”
En la fiesta de anoche ___ al hermano de Facu.
B.why: A first meeting is one event: conocí.

B.q: Which sentence tells it right? “It was late when the taxi arrived.”
o: Era tarde cuando el taxi llegó.
Fue tarde cuando el taxi llegaba.
B.why: The time is the scene (era); the taxi arriving is the event (llegó).

postcard: Write a postcard (3 to 5 sentences) about a real trip or outing of yours: what happened, and what it was like.

rubric.detail: Weather, feelings, what was going on, in the imperfect

rubric.title: Picks the right meaning
rubric.detail: Uses tenía/tuvo or conocía/conocí for what they mean

rubric.title: A reader understands it
